Remark
1. Remark 1.2\group three-manifolds Source: chow-knopf-ricci-flow:page-0016 Seifert's original definition of a fiber space required the existence of a fiber-preserving diffeomorphism of a tubular neighborhood of each fiber to a neighborhood of a fiber in some quotient of $S^1 \times D^2$ by a cyclic group action. Epstein later showed that if a compact $3$-manifold is foliated by $S^1$ fibers, then each fiber must possess a tubular neighborhood with the prescribed property. Hence the simpler definition given in the text is equivalent to the original.
